summary: England beat Scotland 6-0 at Hampden Park in the Women's Nations League, but the Netherlands scored a fourth against Belgium in added time to win the group on goal difference. England therefore miss out on a Team GB place at the Paris Olympics. Lauren James starred, but earlier dropped points against the Dutch and Belgium proved decisive.
one_line: England beat Scotland 6-0 in the Nations League, but a late Dutch goal against Belgium denied them top spot and a Team GB Olympic place.
key_facts: England scored six goals against Scotland at Hampden Park but it was not enough to overhaul the Netherlands on goal difference.
The Netherlands scored a fourth against Belgium deep in added time (the 95th minute) to secure top spot in the group ahead of England.
England's earlier results hurt them: a 2-1 loss to the Netherlands in September, a 3-2 defeat in Belgium in October, and two poor goals conceded against the Dutch at Wembley.
The first goal England conceded in Utrecht appeared offside in the buildup.
Beth Mead returned to England's starting lineup for the first time since an anterior cruciate ligament injury just over a year earlier; Esme Morgan replaced Jess Carter.
Pedro Martínez Losa changed four players from the side that drew 1-1 with Belgium, with Lee Alexander replacing Sandy MacIver in goal.
England are ranked fourth in the world and Scotland 23rd.
Lauren James scored England's third goal with a curling effort into the top corner, and also set up Beth Mead's goal at the end of the first half.
England's second goal came when a James shot took a heavy deflection and wrongfooted Lee Alexander.
Fran Kirby turned in England's fifth after Georgia Stanway beat Rachel Corsie to the byline.
Mary Earps made an added-time save from substitute Martha Thomas to keep England in it.
Lucy Bronze headed in a late goal, but the Dutch scored in the 95th minute while England players huddled awaiting the other result.
Sarina Wiegman had urged her players to "go wild from the first minute" against Scotland.
Lucy Bronze called accusations that Scotland might feel conflicted over Olympic qualification "the rudest thing I've ever heard", and Rachel Corsie called them "disrespectful" and "outrageous".
